final_lessons: For this bigram LM with RMSprop lr 1e-4 and L1, the compact 2-layer d_model 64 transformer beat larger and deeper variants.
At fixed RMSprop lr 1e-4 and L1, d_model 64 with 2 layers stayed best, while d_model 128 degraded as layers increased.
Very compact d_model 32 can beat d_model 128 variants under RMSprop plus L1, but prior d_model 64 results still look strongest.
The d_model 64, 2-layer, d_ff 256 transformer is a reliable winner over d_model 128 variants with this fixed RMSprop/L1 setup.
For this simple bigram LM, a 1-layer d_model 64 transformer can beat deeper d_model 64 and d_model 32 variants under RMSprop plus L1.
A d_model 64 transformer remains preferable to d_model 128 even with d_ff 64, reinforcing that width 128 is overkill for this setup.
Even a 3-layer d_model 64 transformer beats 3-layer d_model 128 models here; avoid d_model 128 whenever d_model 64 is present.
When using d_model 32, a wide d_ff 256 feed-forward layer helps substantially and can outperform narrower d_model 32 variants.
The 1-layer d_model 64, d_ff 128 transformer is the best observed architecture so far, beating deeper d_model 64 and all d_model 128 options shown.
A d_model 64, 2-layer, d_ff 64 transformer beats shallow d_model 32 and d_model 128 choices, so d_model 64 remains the safest width.
